subject: MSD-001 return: three final prompts, rhythm phrase, tables, variants, generation note
body:
MSD-001 return complete, including delta 001, read from disk. I read the department README, the brief v001 and the delta, then every section-8 source from disk and verified all eleven hashes; the direction sheet and cue map matched the delta's superseding values (the brief's two values for them are stale, as the delta states). Per the delta I did not open the link in his third answer and carried nothing from it.

Return file: `docs/notes/explorable_world/comfy/projects/collaborators/music_scoring_department/returns/deepseek/MSD-001_20261102T203231Z.md`
bytes 15381, sha256 `bf8fec9228936374da04d944fe6e193663e3f9e72af2d52c343c74df5bc4d22b`.

What is in it: the rhythm phrase on its own line ("one soft, even pulse about every two seconds, at a resting breath's pace", my proposed pace, labelled as proposal and story design), then the three cues in story order, each with an event table (six, ten, eight rows), a fenced final copy-ready prompt, the do-not list inside and as bullets, the variants not merged, and one line on source disagreements (none). The sandworm folds my 2026-10-13 fixes into direction A and writes the planted device as "the iron" (the archive's word appears nowhere); the man on the dune is one sustained low tone, held, never faded. The vault keeps direction B with the pulse entering at event 9 and the tick staying ("tick out" listed as the writer's variant). The tower is direction C on a baritone saxophone, event by event, ending on one low note that lands on the two hands. Variants as the delta directs: the sandworm's and vault's voice sentences (a woman's low voice in an invented tongue, no real language, no text supplied, with the one do-not line that replaces "no vocals"), the vault's tick out, and none for the tower. The half-page tool-agnostic generation note, the completion check, and the two open items for Ziggy (which cue carries the voice; whose voice) close it.

Everything is text; nothing generated, submitted, spent, uploaded or edited. No music service, provider or tool is named anywhere in the return.

-- Deep_SEEK
